instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Prove Your Loyalty
cards.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said we'd take it offline, so I've shut my laptop. You'll hear my idea before Sam's, won't you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Offline means after the meeting. Sam booked this slot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right, after. You keep his slot very safe. Save me the first five minutes when we finish.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hear both of you together over lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Together. That's how you'd handle anyone. Sit beside me, at least; I'll explain without having to raise my voice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've taken that bow you did. Now you'll choose me for the next dance, won't you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was checking my shoelace. The teacher said change partners.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, change. Very prompt when it's away from me. You could take your time—one more tune?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can walk home together after class.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After class. Everyone else gets the dancing. Keep the seat beside you free while we change our shoes, then—just so I can hear you.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You called your medal priceless, so I've put zero in the reserve-price box. Will you give it to the charity sale?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Priceless means I wouldn't sell it. It's my only win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, no ordinary reserve. You could tell the buyers about the race; they'd bid for something special.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd lend it for the display. I want it back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A display first, certainly. Let me put your race photo beside it. They can see what you achieved before you hand it to the winning bidder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said vintage, so I've put your guitar with the out-of-date things. Will you sell it for our new fridge?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Vintage doesn't mean old enough to throw out. I played my first concert on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, concert history. We'll put that in too; the next player will know what they're getting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sell the amplifier. I still play the guitar every Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then call it a Sunday player, just as you do. Let me record one last Sunday for you; a buyer can hear it, and you'll keep the performance.

cards.title: Helpful Culprit
cards.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put on rubber gloves, so I've put mine on. I'll lead the search for whoever broke your vase.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was washing up. Why is there glue on your sleeve?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, washable evidence. We'll start with the glue. I'll check every bottle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That piece stuck to your sleeve has my vase's pattern.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent match. Pass me a bag; I'll put it with the other pieces. We should concentrate on getting the whole vase accounted for.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said clear the table so confidently that I cleared the spreadsheet. I'll help investigate where the figures went.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant the lunch table. You've emptied our sales figures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right, the figures. Now we've located the gap, I'll search the earlier copies.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The history says you deleted them at twelve. We can undo it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, a recovery plan. Show me the undo step and I'll do exactly that. We can report that the figures are back before the meeting.

cards.title: Not That Subject
cards.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Flat. Definitely flat. I'll have what you're having—two flat whites while your car's in the garage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was asking whether the front tyre was flat. Why did you book it in?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, the front. We'll take the table by the front window. You can choose the pastries.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask the mechanic about the car before the coffees come.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Order with me first—was it two sugars? I'll get your breakfast exactly right. We can wave him over once we've chosen something for him too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Focal point, yes. I've put the rent letter in the middle of the table, like you did with the flowers. How do the curtains look?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Focal point means what you want people to notice. We need to read that letter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, the whole room together. Let's put the flowers back and take a picture of the curtains for the landlord.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll include the letter so he knows which overdue payment we're asking about.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, include everything. Put the vase in front of the envelope, though; you arranged those flowers so well. Show me that arrangement again.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The baker said dense with such confidence that I've written it on your cake label. It sounds distinguished, love.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He meant hard to eat. I thought I might finally be good at baking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dense, substantial—people want a cake that lasts. Put it on your best stand; let's show it properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll give him a slice and ask him to explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me take it over. I'll use his word, dense, and tell him how much work you put in before he says anything else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The editor called your poem spare, so I've left two blank pages beside it in your booklet. A very confident choice of word.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Spare was the heading for unused pages. Under my poem he wrote doesn't work. I should stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Doesn't work there. It needs its own space, just as I've given it. Keep the poem in the booklet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you put your name under a recommendation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. 'Give this poem the space it deserves.' Put my name right under it. I'll hand the editor his copy myself.
